themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints in CD 402 spiked to 19 THIS WEEK, a 176% increase from the 6.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden enforcement gap or new dumping activity targeting the district.
evidence: 19 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.47)
176% spike in a single week indicates sudden acceleration, not gradual trend
No corresponding Reddit or CB discussion yet, suggesting residents may not yet have organized response
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about what triggered the spike and whether additional enforcement is deployed
Map hotspots: are dumps clustering in specific neighborhoods (e.g., near waterfront or industrial zones)?
Talk to residents on affected blocks about health/safety impacts and how long dumping has been occurring

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 967% spike from the 0.4 weekly baseline over 8 weeks, signaling either new enforcement activity, a wave of non-compliant dining sheds, or resident backlash against existing installations.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49)
967% increase suggests either concentrated problem (specific block, cluster of violators) or new inspection initiative
Post-pandemic outdoor dining remains contentious citywide; CD 402 may be flashpoint
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks/restaurants are drawing complaints and what violations are cited (obstruction, noise, sanitation)
Interview CB or local business groups about whether there's pressure to remove or regulate sheds
Check with DOE (outdoor dining regulator) on whether CD 402 is under special audit or enforcement push

themes_detail.label: Encampment Growth in Sunnyside
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 36 last week, a 433% increase from the 6.8 weekly average, indicating a rapidly worsening homelessness crisis or concentration of unsheltered individuals in the district.
evidence: 36 encampment complaints last week vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.9)
433% spike suggests either rapid population growth or resident complaint surge triggered by visibility/safety concerns
Long-standing CB budget request for parks/amenities; encampments may be occupying public spaces CB wants developed
reporting_angles: Ground-truth the spike: visit known encampment sites (parks, transit hubs, underpasses), count tents, interview unhoused residents on what brought them to CD 402
Interview NYPD/Parks Enforcement on whether they're conducting sweeps or newly allowing encampments
Connect to city shelter capacity: is CD 402 seeing overflow from full shelters or deliberately directed outreach?
Profile a few affected residents: employment status, barriers to shelter, what services exist locally

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints reached 14 last week, an 833% spike from the 1.5 weekly average, indicating widespread sidewalk deterioration or a sudden inspection wave targeting CD 402's pedestrian infrastructure.
evidence: 14 curb condition complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.21)
833% spike is among highest z-scores in dataset, indicating extreme statistical deviation
Complements long-standing CB budget request for street/pedestrian infrastructure investment
reporting_angles: Walk high-complaint blocks to photograph damaged curbs; document severity (trip hazards, ADA violations, aesthetic blight)
Query DOT database on recent street resurfacing work—are complaints tied to poor repairs or deferred maintenance?
Interview CB about whether this is a known issue area or a new shock; check if it's tied to specific street(s)

themes_detail.label: Noise Spike, Particularly Residential
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints jumped to 49 last week (172% spike from 18.0 weekly average), with residential noise also elevated, suggesting either construction activity, new venues, or concentrated nightlife disruption in the district.
evidence: 49 noise complaints last week vs. 18.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.06)
172% spike; residential noise category also elevated (824 complaints over 90 days)
No specific Reddit or news coverage yet, but pattern suggests emerging frustration among residents
reporting_angles: Survey recent DOB permits: are there new construction sites or demolitions underway in high-complaint areas?
Identify noise sources: bars/restaurants, construction, traffic, MTA facilities (subway, bus depot)
Interview residents on complaint-heavy blocks about timing, frequency, and impact on sleep/quality of life
